# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48 (Bu-Vb Pc48)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc48  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48  
**Title (English, from literature):** Going to see a mobilized army  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In modern analysis, Michael Radich highlights Pācittiyas 48–50 as barring even passing contact between the monastic Saṅgha and armed forces, reading military institutions as an arm of the broader socio-economic structure from which monastics withdraw [Radich 2007]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule is widely attested across early Vinaya traditions. Within Pali literature, it directly corresponds to *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* Pācittiya 48 and *Parivāra* Pācittiya 48, with counterpart disciplinary provisions for nuns found in *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* Pācittiya 129, the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. Parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā*.
